findings.text: Low page-table bit positions run from zero for present through eight for global, covering writability, user access, write-through, cache disable, accessed, dirty, large-page selector, and global in ascending order.
High feature bits use fifty seven and fifty eight for programmer use, fifty nine through sixty two for protection keys, and sixty three for no-execute, with large PAT at twelve.

Several logical flags alias shared positions: special and CPA test share the first software slot, userfaultfd shares the second, software-dirty and four-K pinning share the third, protection-none shares global, and small-page PAT shares bit seven.

Saved-dirty and no-PTI-shadow selectors have two mutually exclusive placements, one tied to the fifth software slot and the other tied to the second software slot, indicating a configuration-dependent layout.

Masks combine individual flag values to describe pkey coverage, dirty tracking including saved dirty, protection-none and no-shadow singletons, cache subsets for normal and large pages, and change-allowed sets for normal and huge pages.

Cache-mode enumeration orders writeback, write-combining, uncached-minus, uncached, writethrough and write-protected from zero to five, with eight total slots, and a helper maps a three-bit index onto write-through, cache-disable and attribute-table positions.

User and kernel protection presets combine present, writable, user, accessed, dirty, global, no-execute, encryption and cache behavior into named read-only, copy, shared, executable and kernel table or mapping variants, with exported kernel variants masked by a default PTE mask.

Early identity-mapping attributes use small integer facts for table, directory and top-level entries, while PFN versus flags separation and PAE page and physical masks define which entry portions hold address versus control data.
Page-level enumeration distinguishes none, four-K, two-M, one-G, five-hundred-twelve-G, two-hundred-fifty-six-T and a count sentinel in that order.

Protection-key rights use one access-disable bit and one write-disable bit per key with two bits per key overall, and the initial rights value has two alternative sources, a fixed zero and a readable stored variable.

Audio firmware interface fixes maximum stream count at twenty five and assigns small numeric task and pipeline identifiers, with output pipelines in a low range, input pipelines in a high range starting near one twenty eight, and a reserved sentinel at the top.
CPU entry-area map size has two alternative size rules, one computed from per-CPU plus count-scaled area minus base, and one fixed to a single top-level directory coverage unit.

Allowed top-level entry bits have two alternative rules, one restrictive combining physical mask with present, write-through, cache-disable and three software slots, and one permissive allowing all bits.

Protection values and paging levels are wrapped in single-member structures for protection, top-level, fourth-level and upper-directory entries, while abstract page-table allocation is represented as a pointer to a page descriptor.

Protection-key management exposes helpers to report enablement and maximum key count, allocate the first free key from a per-address-space bitmap, test allocation excluding the reserved execute-only key, and release a key, with negative results signaling absence or exhaustion.

PKRU control exposes a conditional writer that skips the privileged write when unchanged or disabled, a default restorer that reloads the initial value, and execute-only and mprotect override resolvers that return defaults when the feature is off and otherwise delegate.
A protection helper returns a copy with the no-execute attribute added, and VM protection-key flags combine four per-key VMA bits.

Execute-only key provisioning starts unassigned, allocates a fresh key on first need, avoids redundant rights updates when read access is already denied, otherwise installs deny-access rights, frees and abandons on failure, then caches the key in the address-space context for reuse.

Mprotect key selection prefers an explicit caller key, then attempts execute-only assignment for pure execute protection, then demotes execute-only mappings back to the default key when execute permission is removed, and otherwise inherits the existing mapping key, with execute-only detection requiring execute-only flags plus matching cached key.

Several flag and mask definitions collapse to zero when their feature is unavailable, including protection-key bits, no-execute and related software slot, software-dirty and swap variants, userfaultfd variants, and an erratum mask that otherwise combines dirty and accessed.

Per-address-space key allocation uses a bitmask where each key occupies one bit, allocation finds the first clear bit after checking for a full mask, and setting or clearing is done through small bitmap update helpers.

Native page-table initialization is aliased to the generic paging initialization entry, and markers advertise presence of write-combining and writethrough protection constructors plus tracking hooks for PFN maps and physical-memory access protection.

The PKRU privileged write requires two companion registers cleared to zero and is relatively costly, so callers must gate it on feature enablement, avoid redundant writes by comparing against the current value, and treat missing-feature builds as no-operation variants.
User protection-key access update is owned elsewhere and referenced only by identifier.
